newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary pledges flood aid for northern neighbours.
newsitem.headline: Hungary pledges flood aid for northern neighbours.

text.p: The Hungarian government on Thursday pledged 350 million forints ($1.8 million) in disaster relief for Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia after a week of devastating flooding in the region.

"The Hungarian government has decided to provide food and pharmaceuticals to the tune of 250 million forints and an additional 100 million forints will be devoted to other expenses such as transportation," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told reporters.

Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz warned on Thursday that predicted heavy rains could trigger even more of the floods that have already killed 46 people and devastated huge areas in the south of the country.
A similar number of people have been killed in the Czech Republic and the country braced for more misery as weathermen forecast renewed heavy rain at the weekend.
River workers emptied dams on rivers in anticipation of another onslaught from the skies.
Kiss said Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn had telephoned Cimoszewicz to offer help and had been told that the immediate need was for water pumps.

"The government therefore decided that within 12 hours we are going to ship 15 high capacity pumps to assist in what the Polish Prime Minister described as the most severe floods not of the century but of the millennium," he said.
The Hungarian parliament on Tuesday gave the go-ahead for public funds to be used to relieve flood victims in its three northern neighbours.
Hungary has been relatively untouched by the deluge, although the Danube rose to its highest level for six years last Friday before subsiding. ($ = 192.3 Hungarian Forints)
